analysis.title: AI quick pulse: Meta 3Q26 results - strong earnings, Muse ambitions, and a new share class (Transformational Innovation Opportunities (TRIO): Artificial Intelligence)
key_insights: Meta 3Q26 revenue and earnings were both ahead of consensus, excluding the previously disclosed USD 9.9bn legal settlement charge.
Advertising revenue was USD 63.1bn, up 26% y/y against a 26% year-ago comparison, two percentage points better than expected. Impressions rose 10% y/y and average price per ad rose 14% y/y.
US and Canada advertising revenue grew 33% y/y, roughly double the growth of most other regions.
Management cited AI gains in content recommendations, ad ranking, targeting and creative tools, including Meta Generative Recommender, GEM ad ranking models and Andromeda infrastructure improvements.

Reality Labs came in a little below expectations. Management is cutting its operating losses from USD 18-19bn in 2026 to USD 15bn in 2027 by redirecting investment to higher-priority AI opportunities.
3Q26 capital spending was USD 34bn (+80% y/y), producing a free cash burn of USD 2bn despite operating cash flow of USD 33bn (+9% y/y as reported, +42% adjusted for the legal settlement).

4Q26 revenue guidance was largely in line with expectations. The 2026 outlook was raised mainly because of the legal charge. Excluding the charge, Meta reiterated that 2026 operating income should exceed 2025 levels.
Management expects to keep investing aggressively in AI infrastructure, model training and product development in 2027, and expressed confidence in sustaining strong revenue growth through 2027.

More than 10 million users in the US and Canada have set up Muse agents. UBS describes Muse as a platform spanning frontier models, consumer agents, enterprise services and connected devices, not only a standalone AI app.

Meta plans to roll Muse out beyond the US and Canada and to commercial customers (content and ad creation tools, API services, enterprise services). Potential revenue streams are commerce transaction fees, premium subscriptions and paid business offerings. Serving Muse is still compute intensive, and management expects efficiency gains.
Full-year 2026 capex guidance was tightened to USD 135-145bn from USD 130-145bn, against Street expectations of USD 139bn. No 2027 capex guidance was given, but spending will remain elevated.

Meta plans a new non-voting Class C common stock, distributed as a stock dividend, which works like a two-for-one split once trading begins in late January 2027. CFO Susan Li said it creates a traded security for capital raising, employee compensation and acquisitions while preserving existing voting power, including Mark Zuckerberg's control.
In its AI TRIO, UBS favors platform and application beneficiaries, and in the enabling layer infrastructure firms with strong pricing power and competitive positioning in their supply chains.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 revenue and earnings beat consensus excluding the legal charge, with advertising 2 points above expectations. Risks are ad market health, AI monetization, competition and execution.

sector_views.rationale: UBS favors platform and application beneficiaries positioned for AI use cases, plus infrastructure firms with pricing power in their supply chains.

earnings_insights: Meta 3Q26 (reported 10/2026): revenue and earnings both ahead of consensus, excluding the previously disclosed USD 9.9bn legal settlement charge. The report gives no EPS figure.
Meta 3Q26 advertising revenue reported at USD 63.1bn, +26% y/y, about 2 points above expectations.
Meta 3Q26 operating cash flow reported at USD 33bn, +9% y/y as reported and +42% adjusted for the legal settlement. Capex was USD 34bn (+80% y/y) and free cash flow was about -USD 2bn.
Meta FY2026 capex guidance is USD 135-145bn (prior USD 130-145bn) versus Street expectation of USD 139bn.
Meta 4Q26 revenue guidance was largely in line with expectations. The FY2026 outlook was raised mainly because of the legal charge.
risk_factors: Management's ability to monetize AI investments.
Elevated capex with free cash flow turning negative in 3Q26.
